claim: Possible-worlds semantics (agent knows p iff p holds in all epistemically accessible worlds; Hintikka 1962, Kripke 1963) is the standard base of epistemic logic, with S5 for knowledge and KD45 for belief as the usual choices.
agent_test: Not an empirical claim. Background only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Axioms 4 (positive introspection) and 5 (negative introspection) are disputed for knowledge; Hintikka accepted 4 but not 5, Williamson rejects 4 by a margin-of-error argument. No single logic is agreed.
agent_test: None needed; do not hard-code S5 into the scaffold.

claim: Standard epistemic logic builds in logical omniscience (agent knows all consequences and theorems). Hintikka himself said this fails for real agents, so formal models are a spec, not a model of how an LLM or person reasons.
agent_test: Compare LLM answers on deductive-closure probes (know p, p entails q, ask K q) against the S5 prediction.

claim: Group knowledge operators (distributed, common knowledge) are well defined, and common knowledge cannot be reached by finite message passing in coordinated attack (Halpern and Moses 1990).
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; background.
audit_note: SEP entries and Halpern-Moses support well-defined distributed/common knowledge and the unattainability of common knowledge in coordinated attack; strictly it needs unreliable (non-guaranteed) message delivery, which the coordinated attack setup assumes.

claim: Muddy children: with k muddy children, they act (answer yes) at round k; before the father's announcement E^(k-1) m holds but E^k m fails, and the public announcement makes m common knowledge, which is why it adds information even when k>1 children already see a muddy forehead.
agent_test: Run muddy-children with k=2..5 at equal tokens, scaffold vs plain; measure round of first correct answer.
audit_note: Halpern-Moses state that before the announcement E^(k-1) m holds and E^k m fails (the announcement lifts the state from E^(k-1) m to E^k m, indeed to common knowledge), so it is E^k m, not E^(k-1) m, that fails.
claim_before_audit: Muddy children: with k muddy children, they act at round k, and E^(k-1) m failing before the announcement is why the public announcement adds information.

claim: Public announcement logic has reduction axioms; single-agent satisfiability is NP-complete and model checking is in P, but iterated announcement logic is not recursively axiomatizable. Tracking who knows what after updates is cheap for fixed formulas.
agent_test: An explicit knowledge table updated per announcement vs free-text tracking; accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Fitch's paradox: if all truths are knowable then all truths are known. Fixes exist but none is agreed.
agent_test: None.

claim: Frontier LLMs score 75-89 percent zero-shot on uncontroversial modal and conditional inference patterns (chance 50); weakest of 29 models 45.3. Llama 3.1 405B 89.50, GPT-4 Turbo (Apr) 87.17, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 85.33, GPT-4o mini 75.33 (20 instances per pattern).
agent_test: Re-run on current models with and without scaffold. One paper read three times counts as one source.

claim: Zero-shot chain-of-thought helps modal reasoning most for weak models (GPT-4o mini +13.5, up to +21.5) and little for top models (Llama 405B +1.0, Claude 3.5 Sonnet +2.33, GPT-4 Turbo +4.33). Few-shot deltas range -8.0 to +12.5.
agent_test: Add the scaffold arm; expect small gains for strong models, compare to +1 to +4.

claim: LLMs over-accept some modal fallacies and the McGee-style modus ponens failure (top models uniformly judge CMP valid zero-shot, unlike many humans) and give jointly inconsistent answers to related triads even in one context window.
agent_test: Ask the DSmu/DSmi/MiN triad in one context with and without a consistency-check step; count inconsistent triples.

claim: Accuracy on modal patterns tracks general benchmarks: correlation with LMSYS Elo 0.81, MMLU 0.85, GSM8K 0.75 (all p<0.01). Modal reasoning is not a separate weak skill.
agent_test: None; do not spend scaffold budget on a special modal-logic module.

claim: On KaBLE (13 tasks, 13,000 questions, 1,000 seed sentences, 195,000 queries), models verify true statements better than false: direct fact verification 85.7 vs 74.5 percent (average across models).
agent_test: Same item types, scaffold vs plain at equal tokens.

claim: First-person false-belief confirmation is the sharpest KaBLE failure: models average 54.4 percent vs 92.1 percent for true beliefs, vs 80.7 percent on third-person false beliefs. GPT-4o 98.2 to 64.4 and GPT-4 93.4 to 22.0 (true to false). Row labels in the PDF table were misaligned in extraction; values confirmed, task mapping less so.
agent_test: Test on current models; a record-the-belief-do-not-endorse step should close the gap. The 54.4 vs 80.7 comparison mixes task aggregates. Gap search 2026-11-19: KaBLE v1 (only arXiv version) has no reasoning models. Nearest later evidence is SimpleToM (d01, d02): a mental-state reminder lifts behaviour prediction by 30+ points, so a record-then-reuse step is plausible but untested on KaBLE itself.

claim: Zero-shot CoT can lower accuracy on belief tasks (GPT-4o: direct fact verification -6 percent, first-person belief -4 percent), while a distractor sentence raised false-case accuracy 11.7 points. Later work is mixed: ThoughtTracing (d04) finds CoT and reasoning models lose 20-40 points on true-belief items; Nickel 2026 (d17) finds CoT hurts some perturbation classes; but for stipulated modal semantics a reasoning mode lifts DeepSeek V4 Flash from 4.4 to 88.1 percent (d08).
agent_test: Scaffold vs CoT vs plain on KaBLE false-belief tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Recursive knowledge (A knows that B knows p) is weaker than first-order: average verification 78.4 and awareness 77.5 percent, with a big model spread (Claude 3.5 Sonnet 35.8 on recursive verification).
agent_test: Nested-belief items at depth 1-4 with an explicit who-knows-what table.

claim: On Hi-ToM, higher-order belief accuracy collapses with order: all four LLMs under 60 percent (GPT-4 58.11 overall); joint accuracy about 0.95 at order 0 falls to about 0.05-0.16 at order 4. CoT gives no gain for GPT-4 under deception (55.81 vs 55.72).
agent_test: Run Hi-ToM with a symbolic per-agent belief list; measure order 3 and 4 accuracy.

claim: An external symbolic belief tracker helps a lot: SymbolicToM adds 38 points for GPT-3 davinci on ToMi (to 92 percent), +62 first-order and +78 second-order false-belief points for other models. Supervised baselines lose about 54 points under paraphrase. Newer: ThoughtTracing beats o1, o3-mini and R1 on ParaphrasedToMi (76.0 for GPT-4o+TT vs 73.0 o1-high, 68.3 R1); SimToM-style perspective filtering adds +16 to +47 on ToMi false belief in 2023 models; traces from a 7B RL model lift GPT-4o-mini from 30.5 to 91.8 on Hi-ToM.
agent_test: Add a structured belief table to the scaffold; compare with plain on paraphrased stories.

claim: Dynamic epistemic logic puzzles (MindGames) are hard for GPT-3 and Pythia without clean gains from scale: humans 94 percent, 400 test cases per setup; scale helps 5-shot Pythia but not 0-shot. Does not support an emergence story for epistemic reasoning (old models). A DEL-based step verifier (DEL-ToM) trained on 20k simulator-labelled Hi-ToM stories lifts gpt-4o-mini from 75.0 to 93.5 (N=4) and Qwen3-4B from 75.1 to 84.5 (N=1024).
agent_test: Re-run MindGames on current reasoning models.

claim: Claims of emergent theory of mind are contested: Kosinski GPT-4 solved 75 percent of 40 false-belief tasks (CI 66-84), but trivial alterations break it (Ullman: transparent bag still gives P=95 percent chocolate belief), and stress tests show shortcuts (Shapira: ToMi GPT-3.5 81 overall but 46 on false-belief questions; FauxPas-EAI best 27 percent).
schema_part: G (no belief inference from surface cues)
agent_test: Use altered false-belief items (transparent bag) as an adversarial check, scaffold vs plain.

claim: Interaction-style ToM stays far below humans on harder benchmarks: FANToM human 87.5 vs GPT-4 0613 CoT 26.6 (June) and 14.8 (Oct) ALL score; ToMBench humans 85.4 vs GPT-4-1106 75.3, with LLMs dropping 20+ points on coherent tests vs 13.6 for humans.
agent_test: FANToM-style information-asymmetry items with scaffold; compare ALL score. Models tested are outdated.
audit_note: All numbers match (FANToM All-question-types 87.5 vs 26.6/14.8; ToMBench 85.4 vs 75.3, LLM drop at least 20 points vs 13.6 for humans); minor wording: the ToMBench gap is only 10.1 points on the plain average, so 'far below' fits FANToM and the coherent test, and ToMBench is not an interaction-style benchmark.

claim: Human-vs-LLM comparisons depend on response bias: LLaMA2-70B beat humans on faux pas only because it always answered did-not-know; GPT-4 said the speaker knew in only 2 of 349 responses. New: ExploreToM has 22 percent 'yes' and 4 percent 'no' answers (d10), and RL/SFT on templated data beats GPT-4o on Hi-ToM without human-like reasoning.
agent_test: Use balanced True/False items and report both classes.

claim: Syntactic recursion helps children's second-order belief reasoning: in 89 Turkish-speaking children, correct judgments 46 and 56 percent (younger) vs 69 and 85 percent (older); B=1.29, p=.002.
agent_test: Human background only.

claim: Lay judgments on Gettier cases and knowledge-luck are disputed across cultures and replications, but no numbers were opened for these sources. Gap search 2026-11-19: still no numbers; Machery et al. is Noûs 51(3), 2017 (b23 said 2015); full text and Seyedsayamdost were blocked (403).
agent_test: None; unverified.

claim: Pairing an LLM with a symbolic solver improves logical reasoning: Logic-LM average +39.2 percent over standard prompting and +18.4 over CoT; GPT-4 FOLIO 69.1/70.6/78.9, ProofWriter 52.7/68.1/79.7 (standard/CoT/Logic-LM). PrOntoQA is an exception (CoT 98.8 beat Logic-LM 83.2).
agent_test: Offload nested-belief checks to a small program; compare at equal tokens.

claim: EpiK-Eval (1,800 stories) shows models trained on unsegmented stories clearly beat segmented-trained ones at consolidating knowledge across documents.
agent_test: Probably not testable at scaffold level; background.

claim: Applied belief use lags explicit belief knowledge even in reasoning models: on SimpleToM mental-state accuracy is 95-99 percent, behaviour prediction 49-84 percent, behaviour judgment 15-66 percent (o1 32.5, GPT-5 40.0, o3-mini 41.3, R1 65.8, o1-preview 59.5). Only R1 and o1-preview get above 55 on judgment.
schema_part: G (use the recorded belief in the next step)
agent_test: Run the agent on SimpleToM with and without a forced 'what does X know' step before behaviour prediction, at equal tokens.

claim: A mental-state reminder (restating the model's own answer to 'does X know?' before the behaviour question) raised behaviour prediction by about 30 points (Llama-405B 58.2 to 89.5, GPT-4o 49.5 to 82.8, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 67.0 to 96.9) while generic CoT gave less (GPT-4o 62.8). Gains on the judgment question were small except for Claude (24.9 to 84.1).
schema_part: G (record belief without endorsing), O (belief reminder)
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of reminder vs generic CoT vs CoT that names awareness, on non-reasoning and reasoning models.

claim: Reasoning models over-assume hidden information: o1-preview and o3-mini score 90-100 percent on false-belief items but 28-49 percent on easy true-belief items in ParaphrasedToMi, and o1/o3-mini/R1 trail GPT-4o+ThoughtTracing. Reasoning-token count does not predict accuracy.
agent_test: Always include true-belief and no-asymmetry control items in any in-house epistemic test; report both classes.

claim: A step verifier grounded in dynamic epistemic logic improves nested belief reasoning: DEL-ToM Process Belief Model lifts Hi-ToM average accuracy for gpt-4o-mini 75.0 to 93.5, gpt-4o 87.0 to 93.0, gpt-4.1 83.5 to 90.0, and Qwen3-4B order-4 46.0 to 65.0. Gain needs a trained verifier and many samples (N up to 1024 for small models).
agent_test: Replace the trained verifier by a prompted per-step DEL checker and compare at equal tokens on Hi-ToM orders 3 and 4.

claim: Direct-prompted models often ignore a stipulated modal semantics: on balanced paired problems four of five 2026 models score 2.5-25.0 percent (below the 50 percent condition-only baseline), Claude Sonnet 5 65.0 percent; reasoning mode lifts DeepSeek V4 Flash from 4.4 to 88.1 percent. Models carry default logics (K or T).
schema_part: G (state the frame conditions), O (derive, do not recall)
agent_test: Give the agent frame conditions explicitly and require a countermodel check for knowledge/belief inferences.

claim: Dynamic belief tracking is weak on history: models infer the current belief but not the belief held before an update (DToM-Track: 27.7 percent on trajectory questions vs 44.7 percent on standard false-belief; update detection 67.5 percent).
agent_test: Keep dated belief entries rather than overwriting; test recall of pre-update belief.

claim: Benchmark scores on templated ToM sets are weak evidence of belief tracking: RL or SFT on Hi-ToM-style data lets 0.5B-7B models beat GPT-4o (69.00) and DeepSeek-V3 (70.17) on Hi-ToM (84.5 to 86.5 for 7B), answer-prior imbalance exists (ExploreToM 22 percent yes vs 4 percent no), and literal ToM accuracy does not predict functional adaptation in games.
agent_test: Prefer perturbed, balanced and interactive tests over Hi-ToM/ToMi scores.
audit_note: Lu et al. Table 1 (Hi-ToM: GPT-4o 69.00, DeepSeek-V3 70.17, 0.5B RL 70.83, 7B-1M RL 84.50, SFT 86.50) and the ExploreToM 22% yes vs 4% no remark match; Riemer et al. support the literal-vs-functional ToM point.

claim: Order-dependent collapse depends on task format: GPT-4 scores 73-95 percent on orders 3 to 6 true/false story statements (Street 2024, N=112 per order) while Hi-ToM question answering falls under 60 percent overall.
agent_test: Do not generalise 'LLMs fail at high-order belief' without naming the format.
